question: Is the Islamic shroud required, and can several people be buried in one grave during a plague?
answer:
We also need to get to the issue of the burial itself. And again, ideally, as I mentioned, the people who study Islamic fiqh and the people who know this, they know that there's a particular shroud and there's a particular mechanism. If we're able to do this, fine, but this is sunnah, by the way; it is not wajib. If you don't have the shroud, even in regular circumstances, as long as the body is covered in some manner, that is the bare minimum. So if we're not able to have the five or seven shrouds, if we're not able to have the white and the way that it is typically done, that is not wajib. And there are many times in history... in fact, even in the Battle of Uhud, multiple people passed away and there wasn't even enough cloth to cover them up. So as long as the body is covered with something (and these days we have the body bags and whatnot), that is not going to be an issue.

However, another issue might come: can we bury multiple people in the same grave, especially if the number of deaths increases and we don't have space? What can we do then? Realize that once again, we don't need to reinvent fiqh. Alhamdulillah, our fiqh discussed these issues many, many centuries ago. And we know that even in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, in the Battle of Uhud, too many people passed away, and so the Prophet ﷺ said, "Bury two or three people together, as many as you can." And so multiple people were put in one grave. There is no problem whatsoever in this regard.

And this is something, once again, that doesn't need any new ijtihad, if the situation gets difficult and we don't have space, or it becomes logistically difficult to keep on digging and burying. And you know, dear Muslims, plagues always brought about this issue in Islamic history. Every time there was a plague, there were some problems with burials, and our scholars overlooked it for the time. No big deal; it happens; what can you do.

So if (and we seek Allah's refuge) the number of deaths increases such that we will not have the time or the logistics or the energy or the space to have every single person buried in one grave, no problem. Our sharia allows this. Even in the Battle of Uhud (and by the way, in the Battle of Uhud they had the time, but it was just time- and energy-consuming), the Prophet ﷺ allowed two or three people to be buried in the same qabr. So how about now, when we might not have the luxury? So no problem. **Multiple people may be buried in one grave if the situation calls for this.**
